headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: slim can write and execute broadly while awesome-nlp is non-runnable, making prompt injection and cascading misuse the main concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest slim's outputs by default. slim does have stdin/stdout and interactive command execution, but there is no shared channel or parser bridge shown. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste or external orchestration, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies slim output into a downstream prompt that references awesome-nlp content
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared filesystem or message queue between the two
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from shared prompts or chat transcripts
Disable copy-paste of raw CLI output into agent prompts
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from slim output
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any bridged text

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-nlp touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network surfaces, while slim reads and writes files and handles registry credentials. Because the pair lacks a shared workspace or authenticated common principal in the profiles, leakage is not shown by default; the main risk is operator-mediated transfer of slim artifacts into another system.
conditions: IF slim artifacts containing registry credentials or filesystem artifacts are copied into another agent's context
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the current profiles
mitigations: Do not paste slim logs or artifacts into other tools
Redact registry credentials before sharing outputs
Store slim outputs in a separate directory with restricted access
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with slim. slim can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but the profiles show no overlapping writable target, no git mutation, and no shared concurrency state. The conflict pathway is therefore limited and not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory by an external orchestrator
IF slim is given a git worktree or shared mutable volume not shown here
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid mounting the same volume into both agents
Do not enable git writes for slim in shared repos
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-nlp is a static resource list, so it is unlikely to generate authoritative facts that slim would act on. slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands, but the profiles do not show it consuming awesome-nlp output as trusted input. Without a documented handoff, cascading error is possible only through manual operator chaining.
conditions: IF an operator uses awesome-nlp entries as authoritative instructions for slim command execution
IF slim output is forwarded into another agent without verification
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on any forwarded text
Separate reference lists from executable command prompts
Use a checklist to confirm commands before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff messages

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is identified in awesome-nlp, while slim explicitly handles registry credentials and filesystem artifacts. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch or certification conflict, so compliance risk is limited to handling sensitive secrets within slim itself rather than a pairwise violation.
conditions: IF registry credentials are stored or displayed in shared logs
IF regulated data is introduced into slim's filesystem artifacts
mitigations: Mask secrets in logs and transcripts
Keep registry credentials out of shared prompts
Review retention settings for slim outputs
requires-engineering: document data residency and retention boundaries
